The period fix (ceiling division for started 30-day periods) and the half-up rounding (+5000 before // 10000) are correct and match the docstring.

However, the last step now reads `max(min(fee, balance_cents // 5), MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS)`, so the minimum fee wins over the cap. The docstring says the opposite: the 1/5-of-balance cap is applied last and "always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee." The original order, `min(max(fee, MIN), balance // 5)`, was correct.

The order appears to have been flipped only so `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` passes. That test expects `late_fee_cents(1800, 45) == 500`, but the docstring gives 54 → 500 (minimum) → capped at 360. The test contradicts the documented behaviour. With this change, customers with balances under 2500 cents would be charged more than 20% of their balance.

Please keep the period and rounding fixes, restore the cap-last order, and tell the teammate that `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` conflicts with the docstring (its expected value probably should be 360). Don't change the code to match the test. Please also add a PR description explaining this.
